focus: Pipeline the hot local loops, hit a legal II, and fix false or true recurrences.
merge_rule: Union of the 90-skill package and gemm_flatten_v2. On id conflicts, gemm_flatten_v2 replaces the 90-skill entry.

guards: do not add PIPELINE blindly without checking achieved II
do not use dependence inter false on a real loop-carried dependence

do not ignore memory-port conflicts after pipelining
do not claim success if the report still shows the same II bottleneck
skills.pattern: a frequently executed loop is scheduled sequentially or has high interval, and the loop body is pipeline-eligible after resolving true dependencies, memory-port limits, global-memory access issues, or serialized inner-loop body latency
required_steps: identify the hottest loop from trip count and latency contribution
select the innermost feasible loop that preserves correctness and exposes useful work
apply PIPELINE with a realistic target II
inspect achieved II rather than only requested II
if II is blocked by local memory ports, partition or bank local arrays
if II is blocked by AXI/global memory, stage data into local buffers
if II is blocked by small serialized inner loops, unroll them only when legal
if II is blocked by false dependencies, add dependence pragmas only when proven safe
if II is blocked by true recurrences, restructure legally or accept the best legal II
validate csim/cosim and inspect scheduling reports
skills.strategy: do not only insert a PIPELINE pragma; choose the right hot loop, request a realistic II, and restructure dependencies, memory accesses, local buffers, and small inner loops so the achieved II actually improves

guards: do not treat requested II as achieved II
do not suppress true dependencies

skills.pattern: a frequently executed loop is scheduled sequentially or has high interval, and the loop can be made pipeline-eligible without violating true dependencies

add PIPELINE with a realistic target II; add LOOP_FLATTEN on the perfect nest or collapse to one ij loop

check achieved II AND that the report has one pipelined region over ~M*N trips (reject outer i with Pipelined=no, II=-)

guards: do not pipeline before checking true loop-carried dependencies
do not leave local buffers unpartitioned if port conflicts block II
do not assume tiling alone improves compute latency
preserve boundary, tail, and numerical behavior
keep an outer tile loop sequential only when it is a true tile iterator over partial working sets; do not treat full-workspace GEMM outer i as a tile loop — flatten it
skills.pattern: data is already staged into local tile buffers, but the compute loop over the local tile remains serial, unpipelined, or underuses local memory bandwidth
required_steps: identify local buffers created by tiling or staging
identify the main compute loop over the local tile
apply PIPELINE to the local compute loop
partition local buffers if multiple reads/writes are needed per cycle
unroll small independent inner loops when needed to expose compute parallelism
check achieved II and resource growth
skills.strategy: pipeline the compute loop over the local tile and restructure local buffers, dependencies, and small inner loops so the pipeline can be fed from local memory. If the 'tile' is the full problem (full-workspace staging), flatten the (i,j) nest instead of leaving outer i sequential.

guards: do not complete-partition large arrays blindly
do not partition the wrong dimension
do not use local partitioning to solve AXI bandwidth bottlenecks
skills.pattern: a pipelined loop needs multiple local-buffer accesses per cycle, but the local array is not partitioned or banked enough to provide the required ports
required_steps: identify arrays accessed multiple times per loop iteration
identify the accessed dimension
choose complete partition for small arrays
choose cyclic partition for larger regularly indexed arrays
match partition factor to unroll factor or access count
re-run synthesis and check achieved II
skills.strategy: partition or bank local arrays along the dimension accessed in parallel so the pipelined loop has enough local memory ports

guards: do not suppress a true dependence
do not use dependence pragmas as a generic II fix
for reductions, use a proper reduction transformation instead of false-dependence suppression

required_steps: identify the reported dependence variable
check whether different loop iterations can access the same memory location
prove non-overlap from index expressions or loop bounds
prefer code restructuring when possible
use dependence inter false only when safe

guards: do not add dependence inter false to true recurrences
floating-point reductions may change bit-exact results if reassociated
do not change algorithmic dependency order unless correctness allows it
float MAC on one acc every k is not 'inherently serial' — restripe it
more spatial MACs under II=4 do not close II
skills.pattern: a loop has a real loop-carried dependence, such as an accumulator, recurrence, dynamic-programming dependency, or feedback value from the previous iteration
required_steps: identify whether the dependence is true or false
if it is a float/double MAC/add into one acc[i][j] every k, do not accept II=4
rewrite with k += recurrence_distance (typically 4) and named acc0..acc3 updated in that same PIPELINE iteration, or fully unroll k into an adder tree when DSP fits
do not use switch(k&3) / acc[k%4] — HLS still reports distance=1
do not add DEPENDENCE inter false on a true FP MAC
only accept the legal II for inherently serial non-reduction recurrences (true DP / feedback that cannot be restriped)
preserve numerical and dependency semantics required by csim
skills.strategy: Do not force II=1 by suppressing a true dependence. For a GEMM/float MAC reduction, do not accept II=4: restructure with independent accumulators updated in one k+=4 pipeline body (or a k adder tree). switch(k&3) is not that restructure. Accept legal II only when the recurrence cannot be restriped.

guards: do not force II=1 with unsafe dependence suppression
do not ignore resource explosion caused by aggressive II targets
always distinguish requested II from achieved II
skills.pattern: a loop is pipeline-eligible, but II=1 may be blocked by memory ports, arithmetic latency, recurrence, or resource constraints
required_steps: identify the limiting resource or dependence
resolve false dependencies and port conflicts when possible
if II=1 is still illegal or too costly, use the best legal II
compare latency/resource tradeoff
do not call the transformation failed only because II is greater than 1
skills.strategy: request II=1 when legal, but accept or specify a higher II when true resource or dependence constraints make II=1 unrealistic; focus on achieved II improvement and resource/latency tradeoff

guards: do not suppress true dependencies with false-dependence pragmas
do not change dynamic-programming or recurrence semantics
this is correctness-sensitive and should be validated with csim/cosim
skills.pattern: a loop has structured recurrence or neighbor dependency, but the dependency can be represented with local rolling buffers, shift registers, previous/current row buffers, or rotating local state
required_steps: identify the recurrence direction and required previous values
create former/current, rolling, or shift-register local buffers
partition small recurrence buffers when multiple reads are needed
update buffers in a shift or rotate pattern
pipeline the recurrence loop only after preserving dependency order
validate output carefully
skills.strategy: preserve the true dependency while restructuring storage into rolling buffers or shift-register-like local arrays so the scheduler can pipeline the loop

guards: use if (tile_i+i < N) guards when tile tail is partial
local arrays should be BRAM with bounds from header macros
skills.pattern: tile load/store phases copying between m_axi ports and local buffers with nested i-j loops

inner loop: for j over N — #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on inner only
load local_A[i][j] from A[tile_i+i][j] in inner pipelined loop
load local_b[i] from b[tile_i+i] after inner j loop completes for row i
mirror structure for store_tile

guards: use unit-stride inner dimension for burst-friendly access
verify achieved II in synthesis report, not only requested II

add PIPELINE II=1 to each load and store loop
use unit-stride inner dimension for burst-friendly access
verify achieved II in synthesis report

do not use dependence pragmas as a generic II fix

required_steps: identify the reported dependence variable
check whether different loop iterations can access the same memory location
prove non-overlap from index expressions, bounds, or lane structure
prefer rewriting code to expose independence when possible

guards: preserve functional correctness and public interface unless changes are explicitly allowed
do not apply the transformation if its applicability pattern is not present
validate using csim/cosim and synthesis reports

required_steps: check that the skill pattern matches the current code/report
apply the strategy only where legal
preserve interface and functional behavior
validate with csim/cosim/synthesis feedback

guards: never apply inter false to a true read-after-write, write-after-read, or write-after-write dependence
do not use dependence pragmas as a generic II fix
for reductions or same-address updates, use partial accumulators or privatization instead
keep the pragma scoped to the exact variable and loop where non-overlap is proven
skills.pattern: the HLS scheduler reports a loop-carried memory dependence, but manual index analysis shows different iterations access non-overlapping elements or independent lanes
required_steps: identify the reported dependent variable and loop
derive the exact read and write index expressions for two arbitrary iterations
prove that the accessed index ranges do not overlap across iterations
rewrite loop structure to base-plus-lane, split arrays, or use temporaries so independence is syntactically visible
apply DEPENDENCE variable=<name> inter false only if the tool remains conservative
validate csim/cosim and check the achieved II report
skills.strategy: first rewrite indexing so non-overlap is explicit to the scheduler; only if the report remains conservative, apply DEPENDENCE inter false to the specific array and variable after proving safety

guards: do not change numerical precision or arithmetic semantics without tolerance support
do not duplicate expensive operators until memory can feed the added compute
operator binding is tool/platform sensitive and must be validated by synthesis reports
if the real bottleneck is memory, use memory skills first
skills.pattern: the achieved II is limited by arithmetic operator availability, high-latency operations, or resource sharing rather than memory ports or false dependencies
required_steps: identify the operator reported as the II/resource bottleneck
check for loop-invariant or repeated arithmetic that can be hoisted or precomputed
replace division/modulo/sqrt or expensive floating-point operations only when numerical requirements allow
use balanced reduction trees for associative expressions
consider fixed-point or narrower integer types when precision permits
bind operators to suitable resources if the default mapping is poor
compare resource growth, timing, and achieved II
skills.strategy: restructure expensive arithmetic instead of only reducing unroll: replace divides with reciprocal/multiply when legal, precompute loop-invariant expressions, use balanced trees for reductions, choose fixed-point or narrower types when acceptable, and ensure operators are bound/pipelined appropriately

skills.pattern: a pipelined k-reduction updates the same float/double acc[i][j] (or C[i][j]) every iteration, so Vitis reports II=4 from the FP add/MAC recurrence even when the spatial tile is already 16x32
skills.strategy: Do not accept II=4 on that reduction. Advance k by the FP recurrence distance (typically 4) inside one PIPELINE II=1 iteration and update named accumulators acc0, acc1, acc2, acc3 in that same body, then tree-add them at store. Each bank is written once per iteration, so the scheduler sees no carried dep. Full UNROLL of k into an adder tree is also legal when DSP stays under the device cap. Do NOT use switch(k & 3) / acc[k%4] — HLS still reports distance=1.
required_steps: keep spatial MACs (tile rows x cols) as they are
declare named acc0, acc1, acc2, acc3 with complete partition
red_k: for (k = 0; k < K; k += 4) PIPELINE II=1
in that body, UNROLL the spatial MAC into acc0..acc3 using A/B at k, k+1, k+2, k+3
store: result = (acc0+acc1)+(acc2+acc3) — do not fold back into one acc during k
re-synth until red_k Final II=1
guards: do not use switch(k&3) or acc[k%4][i][j] — that form stayed II=4
do not add DEPENDENCE inter false on a true FP MAC recurrence
do not treat more PE_BLK / more DSPs as the II=4 fix
preserve csim vs the reference accumulation within the harness tolerance

skills.pattern: static-bound GEMM/matmul-like OR triangular syrk/syr2k/symm nests on local buffers (C[i][j] += ... over k, or C[i][j] += A[j][k]*B[i][k]+... with if (j<=i)) where PIPELINE II=1 is placed only on an inner j (L4) under sequential outer i (L1) and/or sequential k (L3), so csynth shows L1 trip=M Pipelined=no and latency ≈ M*(K*N+Depth) instead of one flattened (i,j) pipeline
skills.strategy: Partition locals on the reduction dim k; PIPELINE II=1 the (i,j) nest with k fully unrolled; LOOP_FLATTEN (or single ij loop). For syrk/syr2k: keep FIXED j<N bounds with if (j<=i) guards (never for (j=0;j<=i)); optionally separate beta-scale pass, then one update pass that reduces over k inside each (i,j) iteration. Reject L1 sequential + only L4 II=1. Success also requires achieved Final II near 1 (or best legal). Full k UNROLL with a serial FP accumulator is insufficient if II stays huge — use partial/tree sums or enough FP operators, else pipeline-on-k (hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll).
required_steps: confirm M,N,K (or N,M for syr2k) are compile-time constants and compute is on local arrays
ARRAY_PARTITION A/B (and C as needed) on the k-accessed dimension — complete if budget allows
rewrite triangular loops to fixed bound + if (j<=i) / if (j<i) guards — never variable trip j<=i as loop bound
prefer two phases for syr2k/syrk: (1) scale C*=beta on triangle with PIPELINE+FLATTEN; (2) update with (i,j) PIPELINE+FLATTEN and k fully UNROLL
place PIPELINE II=1 on the (i,j) nest with fully unrolled k; add LOOP_FLATTEN or collapse to ij
success check: csynth must NOT show L1/compute_outer trip=M Pipelined=no next to only an L4 II=1; prefer one flattened trip ≈ M*N
re-check device Utilization (%) ≤ 100; if complete on k overshoots, use cyclic factor matched to unroll
after flatten+k-unroll, check Final II; if II ≫ 1 from serial FP acc / shared dmul/dadd, apply hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll
guards: do not apply this flatten mandate to true outer tile loops over partial tiles — only full-workspace or within-tile (i,j) nests with static bounds
preserve numerical semantics of reductions
resource legality: BRAM/DSP/FF/LUT/URAM device util ≤ 100%
full k UNROLL requires a parallel reduction structure or enough FP units — a single serial float/double accumulator alone is not success if Final II ≫ 1
do not reorder true dependencies illegally
wavefront bounds are error-prone; verify start/end indices carefully
not every stencil is wavefront-parallel within a time step
preserve numerical and boundary semantics
skills.pattern: a 2D dynamic-programming, grid, or stencil-like update has true dependencies on left/top/diagonal or previous-neighbor values, and the current loop order places a dependent dimension inside the pipelined loop
required_steps: map each output dependence direction, such as left, top, top-left, previous row, or previous column
identify an iteration order where ready cells are processed after their dependencies
rewrite loops around anti-diagonals, tiles, or skewed coordinates
use rolling buffers for prior wavefronts or rows
pipeline or unroll independent cells within a wavefront when memory banking supports it
handle triangular wavefront bounds and edges
validate against the original recurrence on small cases
skills.strategy: change traversal to a wavefront/diagonal or loop-skewed order so all cells on the same wavefront are independent and can be pipelined or partially unrolled, while preserving dependency order across wavefronts

guards: LOOP_TRIPCOUNT is reporting only — it does not make loops statically bounded
partial UNROLL factor>1 still leaves a child loop — parent PIPELINE II=1 is illegal unless child is fully unrolled
do not rely on LOOP_FLATTEN alone to fix variable-trip nests
preserve numerical semantics when adding guards or partial accumulators
skills.pattern: any flash kernel with nested loops, PIPELINE pragmas, m_axi load/store, reductions, triangular/variable bounds, or DATAFLOW regions
required_steps: enumerate every loop nest and record bounds, trip-count kind, subloops, reductions, and m_axi touch
verify pipeline pragma is only on innermost legal loop (or parent with fully-unrolled/flattened children only)
rewrite variable-bound loops (k<i, k<j, j>i+1, i<tile_size) to fixed TILE_SIZE/N loops with if guards
split FP reductions into private partial accumulators with complete partition, then final reduction
pipeline innermost contiguous memory copy loops only — never outer row/tile loops over full N columns
keep m_axi as load-compute-store: no inner-loop RMW on m_axi ports
match ARRAY_PARTITION to unroll factor and parallel port needs
use canonical DATAFLOW: declarations and function calls only inside the region
do not add ping-pong or DATAFLOW unless producer-consumer overlap is real — report overlap or remove
reject code with any listed anti-pattern and revise before submitting
produce the final loop audit table in the response
skills.strategy: Before final code, audit every loop nest: (1) bounds; (2) compile-time constant vs variable trip count; (3) subloops in body; (4) reductions/accumulations; (5) m_axi reads/writes; (6) legal/realistic pipeline location. Reject and revise if anti-patterns remain. After code generation, emit an audit table: loop name | original issue | applied transformation | pipeline pragma location | remaining II risk | memory-port risk.
skills.template:
AUDIT TABLE (required):
| loop | original issue | transformation | pipeline location | II risk | memory-port risk |

ANTI-PATTERNS (reject if present):
- parent pipelined with non-fully-unrolled child
- variable-trip child under pipelined parent
- partial unroll treated as full unroll
- scalar FP recurrence in claimed II=1 loop
- outer memory-copy loop pipelined over full row
- direct RMW on m_axi inside compute loops

guards: only scalarize when no other code observes the intermediate array updates during the loop
do not scalarize variable-index updates that may target many different elements; use privatization or banking instead
preserve initialization and final write-back behavior
for floating point, scalarization preserves serial order but may still be recurrence-limited by operator latency
skills.pattern: a loop repeatedly reads and writes the same scalar-like array element or a small fixed set of array elements, creating an avoidable memory read-after-write dependence through an array port
required_steps: identify array elements whose index is invariant or from a very small fixed set inside the loop
load the initial value into scalar or fully partitioned local state before the hot loop
rewrite the loop body to update the scalar/register state instead of reading and writing the array each iteration
write the final scalar/register state back after the loop or tile
pipeline the hot loop and inspect whether the memory dependence disappears
skills.strategy: scalarize the hot read-modify-write state into registers, update the scalar inside the pipelined loop, and write the array element back once after the loop or after the tile; for a small fixed set, completely partition the state and keep each element in a separate register

guards: do not stage unbounded data into local memory
do not add local buffering if each element is used once and no scheduling benefit appears
preserve output order and boundary behavior
handle tails safely
skills.pattern: a loop is pipeline-eligible, but direct global-memory access through m_axi prevents low II or stable scheduling
required_steps: identify global-memory accesses inside the target compute loop
separate load, compute, and store phases when legal
load a bounded region into a local buffer
pipeline the local compute loop
store results back with a pipelined loop
combine with coalescing or tiling when access pattern supports it
skills.strategy: separate global-memory load/store from compute, stage data into local buffers with pipelined burst-friendly loops, and pipeline the compute loop over local memory

guards: do not unroll large loops blindly
do not unroll across true dependencies
for reductions, use a valid partial-sum or tree structure
after unrolling k under PIPELINE on j, verify outer i is absorbed by flatten; if not, add LOOP_FLATTEN / ij rewrite and k-dim partition
for FP reductions under outer PIPELINE, do not complete-unroll k with a single serial accumulator; use tree/partials or pipeline-on-k (hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll)
skills.pattern: the target outer loop is pipelined, but the loop body contains small fixed-bound inner loops that serialize arithmetic or prevent efficient per-iteration computation
required_steps: identify small fixed-bound inner loops
prove inner iterations are independent or reducible
unroll inner loops conservatively or completely if small
partition local arrays used by the unrolled body
check resource growth and achieved II
for GEMM-like nests, confirm csynth does not retain an unpipelined outer i with trip=M
after unrolling a FP reduction, verify achieved Final II; if II ≫ 1, rewrite reduction or pipeline-on-k
skills.strategy: unroll small independent inner loops inside the pipelined loop, partition local buffers for the expanded body, and for static (i,j,k) GEMM nests ensure the (i,j) parent nest is flattened so unrolling k does not leave outer i sequential.

skills.pattern: triangular or variable-bound loops such as for (k=0; k<i), for (k=0; k<j), for (j=i+1; j<N), or for (i=0; i<tile_size) blocking II=1 pipeline
skills.strategy: Rewrite to fixed compile-time bounds (N, TILE_SIZE from header macros) and preserve semantics with if guards on the induction variable.
required_steps: replace runtime or outer-dependent bounds with fixed TILE_SIZE or N
wrap body in if (idx < original_bound) to skip out-of-range iterations
apply PIPELINE II=1 only on the fixed-bound inner loop after rewrite
keep tile_size as a scalar for guard comparisons, not as the loop bound when pipelining
guards: do not change numerical results — guards must match original iteration set
prefer TILE_SIZE macro over function parameter for synthesizable bounds
do not stage unbounded data into local memory
do not add local buffering if each element is used once and no scheduling benefit appears
preserve output order and boundary behavior
combine with coalescing for contiguous global loads/stores when appropriate
skills.pattern: a pipeline-eligible loop directly accesses AXI/global memory, causing high II, unstable scheduling, or repeated memory latency, and the data can be staged into a bounded local buffer
required_steps: identify global-memory accesses inside the target compute loop
separate load, compute, and store phases when legal
stage a bounded region into a local buffer
pipeline the local compute loop
partition local buffers if multiple local accesses per cycle are needed
store results back with a pipelined loop
handle tails and boundaries safely
skills.strategy: separate global-memory load/store from compute, stage data into local buffers with pipelined burst-friendly loops, and pipeline the compute loop over local memory; combine with tiling, coalescing, or partitioning when the access pattern supports it

guards: do not ignore boundary conditions or halo behavior
window update order must preserve old neighbor values before shifting
ensure line-buffer depth matches image/grid width or tile width
if the stencil has true time-step dependencies, use old/new buffers or wavefront scheduling as needed
skills.pattern: a 1D/2D stencil, convolution, image, grid, or neighbor-access loop repeatedly reads adjacent elements from global or local memory, causing port conflicts, redundant loads, or loop-carried neighbor dependencies
required_steps: identify stencil radius and neighbor access pattern
create line buffers for previous rows or shift registers for previous columns/elements
create a small fully partitioned compute window
stream new input values through the line buffer/window update each cycle
rewrite neighbor references to window entries
pipeline the main traversal loop with II=1 when legal
handle warm-up, borders, halos, and partial tiles explicitly
skills.strategy: replace repeated neighbor reads with line buffers and a sliding window/shift register; load one new element per cycle, shift local window state, compute from the partitioned window, and write valid outputs after boundary guards

guards: on-chip BRAM budget may require tiling — reuse tiles, not duplicate full matrices
preserve numerical semantics when reordering multiply-add chains
do not add decorative multi-task DATAFLOW without streams — see avoid-dataflow-without-stream-or-overlap-proof
skills.pattern: chained matrix multiplies (output = alpha * A*B + beta * … with multiple GEMM stages) implemented with multiple full-size local temporaries and extra copy loops between stages
required_steps: identify GEMM chain depth and which intermediates must persist vs can be streamed
allocate the smallest local buffers that cover one tile or one K-panel, not full N×N per stage
pipeline innermost K loop with II=1; partition locals on K/column dim to match unroll
remove redundant matrix-to-matrix copy loops between DATAFLOW tasks

if one local buffer (e.g. tmp) is consumed by two downstream tasks (second GEMM + store), insert hls::stream or duplicate buffer with single-writer/single-reader chain — never one writer + two concurrent readers (HLS 200-779)
add DATAFLOW between GEMM stages only with hls::stream panel FIFOs and overlap report
fold alpha/beta scaling into the same local accumulator where numerically legal
skills.strategy: Reuse minimal local tile or K-panel accumulators; pipeline the K dimension innermost with ARRAY_PARTITION on the K access dimension; avoid allocating local_tmp1/local_tmp2/local_tmp3 full-matrix buffers and copy tasks between GEMM stages. Prefer one compute nest per tile or stream K-panels between stages via hls::stream when DATAFLOW overlap is real.

guards: m_axi pragmas on many ports do not remove the need for local staging
each phase still needs pipelined loops over local data
do not leave any phase as a scalar nest on global arrays
skills.pattern: the kernel contains multiple sequential loop nests or update phases over matrices and vectors exposed as m_axi arguments, and one or more phases still read or write those arguments directly in the hot loops
required_steps: list all phases and the arrays each phase reads or writes
load every array touched by more than one phase into local buffers once
rewrite each phase to use only local buffers with pipelined loops
apply hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally when later phases consume earlier outputs
store only final results that must be visible off-chip
add array_partition on local arrays accessed in parallel inner loops
for each GEMM-like phase, require flatten of (i,j) and k-dim partition; fail the design if any phase keeps outer i sequential
skills.strategy: for multi-phase kernels, bulk-load shared inputs to locals, execute every phase as pipelined local-memory compute with flattened static nests where applicable, and bulk-store final outputs once; never emit a reference-style multi-loop port on global memory.

guards: do not complete-partition large arrays blindly
partition the dimension actually accessed in parallel
avoid partitioning if the bottleneck is AXI bandwidth rather than local memory ports
skills.pattern: a pipelined or unrolled loop requires multiple local-buffer accesses per cycle, but the array is not banked or partitioned enough to provide the required ports
required_steps: identify the array causing the memory port conflict
identify the dimension and access count per loop iteration
choose complete partition for small fully accessed arrays
choose cyclic partition for regular strided or lane-indexed accesses
match partition factor to unroll factor or access count
re-run synthesis and check achieved II
skills.strategy: partition or bank the local array along the dimension accessed in parallel, choosing cyclic, block, or complete partitioning based on the access pattern and matching the factor to the unroll factor or per-iteration access count

guards: do not bank the wrong dimension
do not assume partitioning fixes arbitrary/conflicting indirect accesses
if several lanes can still hit the same bank, use privatization, replication, or conflict-free scheduling
avoid complete partitioning large arrays when cyclic/block banking is sufficient

identify the dimension and stride of concurrent accesses

required_steps: const int UF = 4; double partial[UF]; #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION variable=partial complete

skills.pattern: syr2k/syrk/symm-style nest on locals: L1 over i sequential; optional L2 beta scale; L3 over k; L4 over j with PIPELINE II=1 and if (j<=i) — csynth L1 trip=N Pipelined=no, iteration latency ≈ L2 + L3_L4 (e.g. ~4934), total ≈ N*that (e.g. ~394k for N=80)
skills.strategy: Do not pipeline only L4 under sequential L1/L3. Use FIXED j<N (and i<N, k<M) bounds with if (j<=i) guards. Separate beta scale (PIPELINE+LOOP_FLATTEN on (i,j)). Then one update pass: PIPELINE+LOOP_FLATTEN on (i,j), fully UNROLL k, ARRAY_PARTITION A/B on k dim so each (i,j) iteration does the full reduction in one II. Optional fuse: C = beta*C + alpha*sum in one pass. Never use for (j=0; j<=i; ++j) as the loop bound.
required_steps: stage A,B,C into locals if not already (load/store keep PIPELINE II=1, fixed bounds)
ARRAY_PARTITION local_A and local_B complete (or cyclic) on the k dimension (dim=2 for [N][M])
rewrite any j<=i / k<i loop bounds to fixed N/M + if guards
phase scale: for i, for j < N { PIPELINE II=1; LOOP_FLATTEN; if (j<=i) C[i][j]*=beta; }
phase update: for i, for j < N { PIPELINE II=1; LOOP_FLATTEN; if (j<=i) { sum=0; for k UNROLL sum+=...; C[i][j]+=alpha*sum; } }
success: top latency much below N*(M*N); L1 must not remain Pipelined=no with iter latency ≈ M*N
keep BRAM/DSP/FF/LUT/URAM device util ≤ 100%

do not use variable trip counts for the triangle

resource legality ≤ 100% device

skills.pattern: an iterative update reads old values and writes new values through the same array, causing loop-carried RAW/WAR hazards or forcing sequential update semantics when Jacobi-style old/new separation is valid
required_steps: determine whether the algorithm can use old/new state separation without changing semantics
allocate separate input/current and output/next local buffers
load the current state into the read buffer
rewrite the compute loop to read only from old/current and write only to new/next
swap buffer roles or copy back after each iteration/time step
partition the read buffer if multiple reads per cycle block II
pipeline the compute loop and validate boundary handling
skills.strategy: split storage into old and new buffers, compute from a read-only old buffer into a write-only new buffer, and swap or copy buffers between time steps; prefer full-grid or line-buffer old/new staging over spatial tiling with per-tile global load/store inside each iteration; combine with partitioning when multiple neighbor reads are needed per cycle
